Moved my grandfather into a care home and set up mail forwarding whilst he was away from the property.

E&M billed my grandfather during this time and obviously he wasn't at the address. The mail should have been forwarded but wasn't for whatever reason. Perhaps the letter was hand delivered?

We went to visit the property to freshen it up for sale and noticed a stack of mail.

From the timeline of events they billed him at the beginning of April and by mid May had already started court proceedings.

The property is a retirement block of flats so most of the residents are elderly.

What on earth are you doing escalating to court in the space of 6 weeks?? This is so devoid of empathy. There are numerous reasons why somebody in a retirement home is a few weeks behind paying a bill.

Of course we rang up to explain the situation - I could supply the care contract, the mail forwarding invoice and the sales listing for the flat to support my story. The person on the other end of the phone however refused to speak to us due to GDPR. Wouldn't even tell us what the bill was for which wasn't fully clear from the numerous letters we had received. Wouldn't even let us pay.

Unfortunately my grand father has dementia and we are in the process of sorting out power of attorney.

How unfortunate that my first and only experience with this company is one of such ruthlessness and cruelty.

Better hope your family stays healthy otherwise you might find they're on the other end of a court case within 6 weeks with a bill that has quintupled.

I had a very poor experience with Evans Halshaw and would not recommend them.

From the point of purchase, the air conditioning in my van never worked. The first time I booked it in to be looked at, I arrived on a Saturday to drop the vehicle off, only to be told that I had apparently cancelled the appointment, which I absolutely had not. This set the tone for the level of organisation and service I experienced throughout.

I returned the vehicle multiple times after that, but they repeatedly failed to diagnose the issue correctly. They insisted it was a battery problem and even attempted to process a warranty claim for a battery, which was rejected as batteries are not covered. They would already be well aware that batteries aren’t covered so I’ve no idea why they even processed a claim for a battery. I was then told I would need to pay for a new battery myself despite nothing being wrong with the battery which has since been confirmed from another garage.

After months of getting nowhere, I took the van to an independent garage, who quickly identified the actual fault as a failed air conditioning compressor. They were also surprised that it had previously been suggested the issue was the battery, which further highlights how far off the original diagnosis was. This is something that would have been covered under my warranty if Evans Halshaw had diagnosed it properly in the first place.

Communication and honesty were also a major issue. On more than one occasion I was told the manager was “on holiday” and no one else could assist, it seemed to be their go to line over the months dealing with them. However, on one of those same days, another member of staff called me and said they had just spoken to the manager, which completely contradicted what I had been told, that the manager was on holiday. This explanation was clearly used to avoid dealing with the issue.

It also took months to obtain the pre vehicle inspection sheet. I was repeatedly told it had been emailed to me when it hadn’t. I only received it after insisting on staying on the phone while it was sent. When I finally got it, the air conditioning section had been left blank.

Overall, this experience has been frustrating and disappointing. Poor diagnosis, lack of organisation, lack of transparency, and difficulty getting basic documentation have made what should have been a straightforward issue unnecessarily stressful.

one_star_reviews.text:
My business had high expectations after a very positive initial meeting, but unfortunately the service that followed was deeply disappointing.

After being handed over to operations, communication was extremely poor from the outset. I had to chase to find out when work was starting, I never had a clear sense of what was being done or why, and when I raised concerns, it became clear that assumptions had been made instead of there being any kind of proper strategy discussion. Reporting was also weak, with little explanation provided, and at one point I was even sent an SEO report for another business.

What stood out most was the complete lack of care and attention. I did not feel valued as a client, and I did not feel there was any proper care taken in how my account was managed.

When I later raised these concerns, the response was effectively that I was on the Bronze package. In my view, regardless of package level, if a client is paying for a service, there should still be a proper standard of care, attention, communication and professionalism at all times throughout the contract lifecycle.

My final issue is that, despite the investment made over the contract period, I have finished this engagement with no clear understanding of what impact the work actually had or what value it delivered, if any at all. That should never be the case with a professional SEO service.

To their credit, they did acknowledge some of the communication and process issues when I complained. However, I was disappointed with how the matter was ultimately handled. Sometimes when a service falls short, the way a company responds can help restore confidence, but I did not feel that happened here.

This review is simply an honest reflection of my experience. Based on that experience, I would not use this company again or recommend them to others.

LSS London feels less like a serious security service and more like a box-ticking exercise designed to extract easy money. I live in a genuinely safe area, yet this company presents itself as if it’s providing some essential layer of protection. In reality, the “service” amounts to little more than a single car occasionally driving around—hardly a reassuring or effective security presence.

For something marketed as neighbourhood security, the effort appears minimal and borderline performative. There’s no visible sense of vigilance, no meaningful engagement, and certainly nothing that justifies the cost. It raises the question of what, exactly, residents are paying for.

What’s even more concerning is the apparent lack of proper training. Requiring just a two-day course to work for the company does not inspire confidence in their ability to handle real security situations. Keeping a neighbourhood safe requires skill, awareness, and preparation—not a rushed introduction that barely scratches the surface.

Overall, it feels like a service built on perception rather than substance. For the price being charged, the value simply isn’t there.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed to be writing this, but I’ve now had to begin legal action against this company.

For context, I run a computer business and have been building custom systems for over 10 years. I’ve also had a business account with CCL during that time, which has generally been fine—though now I’m starting to think that may have been down to luck.

Recently, I built a custom system for a customer and purchased an RTX 5080 from CCL for around £1,500. Once all parts arrived, I installed the GPU, but the system would not boot. The motherboard flagged a VGA fault.

As part of our standard process, we tested the system thoroughly using known working GPUs on our test bench. Everything else passed without issue, clearly indicating the GPU was faulty.

I contacted my account manager, who arranged an RMA and a courier collection. The GPU was carefully repackaged in its original box, placed inside a shipping box with additional protective materials, and sent back securely.

CCL received the item on Monday 20th April. After that, I heard nothing. It took three phone calls and multiple emails before I finally got a response—and this is where the experience went downhill.

The customer service representative I spoke to was dismissive and argumentative from the start, despite me making it clear I was simply looking for answers. I was then told the GPU had been opened, tampered with, and damaged.

This is completely unacceptable. As a business, we follow strict QC procedures and do not tamper with hardware in this way. I explained this clearly, along with the fact that we had already confirmed the GPU was faulty before return. Despite this, they refused to take responsibility and instead attempted to shift the blame onto us.

As of today, we have formally issued a Letter Before Action and are prepared to pursue this through the small claims court if necessary. We have full evidence, including images, to show the condition the item left us in, which does not match the claims being made.

At this point, I have serious concerns about how this situation has been handled. From lack of communication to outright accusations, this has been a very poor experience.

one_star_reviews.text: Myself and a friend visited at what must have been just before or dead on 4pm as the door was still open. Granted we failed to observe the opening times and, on later revelation, they did close at 4pm so that is on us but not realising was an honest mistake and we do apologise for it. However, we started browsing and a lady there came right up to us, blocking our path, and just stared at us not saying anything. At first I thought she was a customer who wanted past and I couldn't understand why she was staring at us with such a look but not saying anything, just sighing. As we moved around her to view the shop, we noticed a man bringing in a trolly of books from outside so we identified that we should be leaving now and made our way to the door, noting we had been in the shop maybe five minutes at the very most. On leaving however, the lady who had been staring at us barked in a very rude manner "We ARE closed". I am sorry we stayed past opening but it was an honest mistake and I don't think the rudeness was justified. We left and I said "thank you for you patience with us" not knowing what else to say in response to the way I'd been spoken to. We genuinely are sorry for coming in at closing and we do apologise but there are a myriad of other ways to politely communicate that you are now closed without being mean or giving us a stare down. The shop itself however is lovely and has a good range of books. There were some interesting botanical books in the window and I really liked the folklore books on display. I do wish I had gotten one as they looked very interesting.

I want to share my honest experience with Cowbell Norford because I found their service both unprofessional and unethical.

On 12th January, I viewed a 3-bedroom detached property and made an offer immediately at asking price. The following Monday, my offer was accepted. I was a first-time buyer and used my own broker and solicitor recommended by the broker. I understood that the seller had a previous sale fall through, which the agent said was why the property was not immediately updated to “Sold STC” or even “Under Offer.” However, this left the property open to other buyers while I was progressing in good faith.

It took about six weeks to finalise my financial documents because I am both self-employed and employed, which I communicated clearly to the agent. My broker submitted the mortgage application on 19th February, and the valuation was carried out on 6th March, with the report returned on 9th March. During this time, the agent Maisie sent an email around 16th February saying the seller wanted to continue viewings if there was no mortgage offer by the end of that week — despite my mortgage already being in progress.

When the valuation came back at £245,000, below the agreed price, I contacted the agent to discuss reducing the price. Two days later, I was told the seller would not accept a lower price and that there was now a “cash buyer” — information I had never been informed of previously. I found this very upsetting and concerning. I made a revised offer, even increasing my deposit and covering some of the shortfall myself, showing my commitment to the purchase.

From mid-March onwards, communication became extremely poor. I chased for updates multiple times via email and phone, sometimes waiting days with no response. Eventually, I was informed that the seller was still deciding, but the final communication came via email only, stating the seller had chosen to proceed with the cash buyer. No one called me to explain or discuss the decision, which I found highly unprofessional.

Throughout this process, I felt ignored and undervalued as a buyer. The handling of my accepted offer, lack of transparency about the cash buyer, and extremely slow, minimal communication were unprofessional and, in my opinion, unethical. After investing so much time, effort, and money, I feel let down and strongly caution others to be careful and protect themselves if dealing with this agency!

To be honest, I feel this reflects poorly on the company as a whole. It’s disappointing, as you would expect a business to ensure its staff maintain a high level of professionalism and communication at all times.

I have used Cowell & Norford on several occasions in the past; however, my recent experience with them has been nothing short of shocking.

The lack of support when I was searching for a new home was particularly disappointing, as no assistance was offered at all. Although my property was listed and sold through them, I later became aware that they had encouraged my buyer to pull out of the sale while attempting to sell them an alternative property.

In addition, my interactions with Christine were unpleasant, as I found her to be consistently rude over the phone.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others to avoid using this company.

**[COMPLAINT] Zen Internet – Broken Promises, No Installation, No Internet, Zero Support**

I'm writing this post because I feel I have no other option left. After days of wasted time, broken promises, and an appalling customer experience, I want to warn others and hold Zen Internet publicly accountable. I will be sharing this post across every major UK forum, review site, and social platform I can find – because no one else should have to go through what I am currently experiencing before they make a decision about their broadband provider.

---

**Why I Chose Zen Internet**

I came across numerous glowing reviews of Zen Internet on forums like this one – praise for their reliability, premium service, and customer care. So when Virgin Media offered to renew my contract at £21/month for 1,000Mbps, I turned it down. Instead, I signed up with Zen Internet at £45/month for Full Fibre 900, trusting the community's recommendations. High-quality, stable broadband isn't a luxury for me – it's a necessity. I run a business from home, and my household relies heavily on connectivity, including multiple smart home devices.

---

**The Broken Promise That Started Everything**

I signed my contract with Zen in early March. Installation was confirmed for on or before 25th March – the exact date my Virgin contract was due to expire. Before committing, I specifically asked Zen's customer service: *what happens if installation isn't completed by the 25th?* I was given an explicit assurance – **repeatedly and emphatically** – that Virgin would NOT cut my service until Zen's installation was fully complete. I made sure to confirm this multiple times precisely because I could not afford to be left without internet.

At midnight on 26th March, Virgin cut my broadband.

---

**What Happened Next**

- **Customer service**: Nearly impossible to reach. Expect to wait upwards of two hours just to get through on the phone – completely unacceptable for any ISP, let alone one charging a premium.

- **Rescheduled to 30th March**: After finally getting through and spending more hours on hold, I was assured – again, with absolute confidence – that an engineer would attend on 30th March. I stayed home all day waiting. No one came.

- **Pushed to 1st April, then 2nd April**: After another exhausting round of calls, I was told the issue had been passed to their "Openreach" team and that I'd receive an update on 1st April. The moment I hung up, I received an email confirming the next update date had already been quietly changed to **2nd April**. Not a confirmed installation date – just another update. All responsibility has simply been passed along the chain.

---

**Their "Solutions"**

When I asked Zen what they would do to help me in the meantime – bearing in mind their error has left me with **no internet whatsoever** – here is what I was offered:

1. **"Buy your own SIM card."** Customer service told me that having no internet was a personal expense and entirely my problem. They would not assist in any way.

2. **A temporary hotspot** – which sounded promising, until they admitted they had **no stock** and could not tell me when any would be available. It could be tomorrow. It could be a week. It could be a year. Those were, genuinely, the words used.

3. **A chatbot** – which, like the phone line, requires you to queue and wait indefinitely regardless.

---

**The Current Situation**

As it stands, I have been without any internet connection for multiple days through no fault of my own. My business has been disrupted. My household is affected. I have spent an embarrassing number of hours on hold or chasing updates – time I will never get back. Every promise made has been broken. Every deadline has been missed. Every so-called solution has collapsed.

I was sold Zen Internet on the strength of this community's recommendations. I paid a premium price for what was supposed to be a premium service. What I received instead is, without exaggeration, one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had.

Avoid this shop.
Shocking customer service and zero respect for people's time.
I have had two terrible experiences with Bikeseven (both in Carlisle and Longtown) that prove this business does not care about customers who want to spend serious money.
First experience (Carlisle branch):I went in planning to buy a Cube Stereo bike worth £4,000. Because it is a massive investment, I asked to try the bike for size. The blonde employee working there became visibly annoyed and rude. Just because my English isn't 100% perfect doesn't give anyone the right to show anger and treat a paying customer with contempt. I walked out and bought elsewhere.
Second experience (Longtown branch):I saw 5 units of the AXA Absolute 9-110 chain lock available on their website.
I specifically called them before travelling to make sure they had 4 units physically on the shelf. The staff member on the phone confirmed they had them. I spent an hour driving in heavy traffic. When I arrived, they couldn't find them!Instead of apologizing, the owner started asking annoying questions like "why do you need 4, isn't 1 enough?". When I explained that I just called 20 minutes ago and was lied to, they kept searching and finally managed to find just 1 single lock. 1 lock instead of the 4 I was promised! When I refused to buy just one, the owner offered no apology for wasting my time, just a sarcastic and dismissive "Bye, cheerio!". They clearly treated me differently because of my foreign accent.Interestingly, right after I left, they updated their website to show "1 in stock" instead of 5. They knew they messed up but chose to be arrogant instead of professional.If you have a foreign accent or expect professional customer service for your hard-earned money – avoid Bikeseven. Order online and save your time.

UPDATE:The owner’s reply is a perfect example of their arrogance. Throwing a meaningless, automatic "sorry" under your breath means nothing when you have just wasted an hour of a customer's time. The truth is simple: your lazy staff member didn't even bother to check the shelf when I called. When I walked into the shop and said I was there for the 4 locks, the staff had absolutely no idea where they even were or where that shelf was!After reading other reviews here, I see I am not the only one – multiple customers have complained about the exact same issue: your website claiming bikes are in stock, but they aren't physically there.On top of everything, it is shameless how you try to use a customer complaint to promote your shop by bragging about selling "hundreds of locks" and calling it an "excellent choice". Focus on your customer service, not free marketing.Trying to blame my language skills and suggesting that I "didn't hear" an apology because of my accent is a pathetic, passive-aggressive personal attack. Instead of taking real responsibility like a professional for your messy stock control, you chose to be dismissive and xenophobic. Total lack of respect for customers.

We went to view a Kverneland rake in early February and agreed to buy it after speaking directly with Richard Evans, the Sales Director. The following day, we called him to confirm the purchase, explaining that we didn’t want payments to start until April but were happy to put down a deposit. He said he would inform the office and send over the invoice.

From that point on, the service was nothing short of appalling.

At the start of April, we tried contacting Richard to follow up on the invoice and the rake, but he repeatedly ignored our calls. We contacted other members of staff at Battlefield Machinery who told us he was “busy” and would call us back. He never did. After multiple attempts over several days, including being told he was out of the office, it became very clear we were being deliberately avoided.

We then went to the farm where the rake was located, only to be told it had already been sold and removed. If there was another interested buyer, we should have been told at the time as we would have bought it there and then. Instead, they chose to say nothing, go back on a handshake agreement, and leave us completely in the dark.

This is not just poor service, it is dishonest and completely unprofessional.

Awful experience at your dealership while discussing the purchase of a vehicle.

I have purchased my last two vehicles from your dealership, which is why I was particularly disappointed by this experience.

When looking around the car I noticed a strong cigarette smell inside the vehicle and raised this with the salesperson. I was initially told that when he had previously been in the car he had not noticed any smell. Later in the discussion, he explained that he had the windows down at the time. He then suggested that the smell I experienced may have been caused by the vehicle sitting in the sun with the windows up, which had “drawn the smell out.” Later in the conversation, I was also told the smell could be removed.

I found these explanations contradictory, particularly as there appeared to be an acknowledgment that a cigarette smell did in fact exist after it had initially been downplayed.

I was also unhappy with the comments made regarding finance options. I was told there was “no point” looking online for better finance deals and that dealerships offer the lowest interest rates, with online searches being described as something mainly used by people who cannot obtain credit elsewhere. Following my visit, I completed my own finance comparison and was able to obtain a significantly better rate elsewhere, which made these comments feel misleading and inappropriate.

In addition, I do not feel the finance figures were presented transparently. I was initially quoted approximately £330 per month without any APR details or clear breakdown of how the figure had been calculated. During the discussion, I was given the impression that my current vehicle was being valued at one price. However, when I questioned the figures further and discussed the possibility of arranging my own finance or topping up my existing loan, it became apparent the actual trade-in value being offered was just over £1000 lower with the total finance amount being close to £16,000 on a £13,500 car. Which again if I hadn't asked for the total amount at what point would that have been disclosed?

Throughout the interaction, I was left feeling as though my questions and understanding were being dismissed rather than properly addressed. As a woman, I found aspects of the conversation patronising and it left me feeling that I was expected not to question the figures or finance information being presented.

Overall, I left feeling that there was a lack of openness and transparency throughout the process, particularly regarding the condition of the vehicle and the financial information being discussed.

I ordered and paid for wall panels from this company on May 3rd. On May 6th, their employee William wrote to me and said the order was being manufactured and would be delivered in 5–7 business days. In the end, he offered me a delivery date of May 16th, a Saturday, because Saturday worked for me to receive the order. That’s already 9 business days. Then William wrote to me saying that unfortunately they don’t deliver on Saturdays and could deliver on May 15th. I agreed because I could take the day off that day.

Then, closer to the delivery date, I emailed William again on May 11th to check if everything was okay. William replied that I needed to wait another 7 business days because the company they buy these panels from for me hadn’t manufactured them yet. And he promised me that the delivery of these panels would definitely happen at the beginning of the following week, May 18th–19th. On May 18th, I wrote to William again to check if everything was okay this time. I was told there were some more delays and that the delivery would definitely not be at the beginning of the week but on Thursday, May 21st. I asked to have the delivery on Friday so I could take the day off. That’s what we agreed on.

On Friday, I was at home waiting for the delivery and decided to call to check roughly what time to expect the order. William was off, and Eddie answered, saying that unfortunately there would be no delivery. Delivery would be on Tuesday, May 25th. What??? I took the day off to receive the order and lost £120 by not going to work. Now they tell me delivery will be on Tuesday – that will be 16 business days since I paid for and ordered these panels.

My wife is pregnant, and I wanted to finish the nursery before the baby is born, but I’ve been waiting almost a month for these wretched 17 panels. It’s not even 100 pieces. What is there to manufacture??? 17 MDF wall panels, 3050mm long – any decent company would have them in stock. I asked this time to leave the order with my neighbors on May 25th, and if they’re not there, just leave it by the door, because I can’t take another day off. I also asked for some kind of compensation, but after my email about compensation, they didn’t even bother to reply to my emails.

I hope the order arrives this time on May 25th, and I hope it arrives without defects. If not, I will take them to court for misinformation, as well as for misappropriation of funds and using my money for such a long time without providing the goods. I have all the evidence in the form of email correspondence. I hope it doesn’t come to that, and I finally receive my long-awaited goods.

Original post :
Having bought it in July 2024, I’ve used it for a total of about 8 hours over 4 months.
Carefully followed the instructions about lubricating the various bayonet joints.
Winterised the unit from Nov to March.
Came to use it and the bayonets will not mate.
Asked Nilfisk customer service who eventually told me “it’s the O-rings - they go hard, you need to follow the link and buy a spare set”.
£18.99.
The entire unit is currently unusable as the spray heads will not attach. And if they do I worry they won’t detach as they are very tight.

Now bearing in mind I have 2 spray heads, an extension lance and a patio head, I need 4 o-rings.  The spare pack has only 2 of that size, so need to buy 2 sets totalling £38.
As the first set has “hardened” after 4 months, I might need to replace them again before end of 2025.  So potentially £76 in seals per year.
I realise seals are “consumables” and not covered by warranty but strikes me as a planned ransom - by fitting poor quality seals that harden within weeks - to keep this prime quality piece of kit working.
Asked Nilfisk to send a set of seals free of charge as a gesture of goodwill. No resposne.
Not impressed. Not happy.
Would not buy another.
My old £180 Spear & Jackson unit may not have the same pressure or flowrate as the Nilfisk P200 but it’s been running for 5 years with bi-weekly use cleaning cars and never needed a spare part or repair.

The Only "Exclusive" Feature is Their Commitment to Failure

​⚠️ HYPOCRITICAL & ARROGANT: Do Not Fall For Their Public "PR" Responses
​Review Update: Notice how "Lisa" has replied below with the classic, sanitised corporate line asking me to call her? It’s pure theatre. I have already called her. I phoned specifically to highlight these exact issues, and the sheer arrogance dripping from her tone on that call was palpable. They love to act accommodating in the public comments to save face, but the reality behind closed doors is a completely different story.
​What is most telling, however, is the sudden shift in strategy. In previous posts, they were quick to deny everything. Now? Lisa wants a chat and completely avoids denying a single point I’ve made. That silence speaks volumes. It’s a tacit admission of guilt wrapped in a fake customer service bow.
​If this business actually cares about resolving this situation instead of just managing their online reputation, they know exactly what they need to do. Stop hiding behind transparent "please call us" templates, drop the arrogant attitude, and fix this.

Rarely does a professional referral lead so directly into a den of such profound incompetence. My experience with Currans was not merely a disappointment, it was an exercise in witnessing systemic laziness masquerading as "prestige" agency.

​An Atmosphere of Unearned Superiority
​Perhaps the most grating aspect of the experience was the staggering level of snobbery exhibited by the staff. They carry themselves with a self-entitled arrogance that their actual performance simply does not support. It is a peculiar brand of "prestige" delusion where the team treats basic client requests as an inconvenience, acting as though they are doing you a personal favor by failing to do their jobs. This condescending attitude would be laughable if it weren't so obstructive.

Logistical Chaos
​Furthermore, their management of viewings was shambolic. Despite explicit promises to arrange viewings in efficient blocks to minimize disruption, they scattered appointments haphazardly across the week. Feedback from the viewers themselves has been damning; one lead confirmed today that the office was agonizingly slow to respond to inquiries, describing the interaction as a total waste of time. Their internal disorganization actively sabotaged potential interest.

Financial and Legal Negligence
The rot set in immediately with a contract riddled with basic arithmetical errors—a "clerical oversight" that would have conveniently cost me an additional £500 in commission had I not performed the due diligence their own team clearly finds beneath them. This was followed by the legal absurdity of attempting to market the property without an EPC, a blunder that isn't just negligent; it’s a statutory breach.

The "Marketing" Myth
The brand’s self-mythologizing is, frankly, hilarious. I was treated to a carousel of tired industry jargon by a representative fresh out of university who possessed a staggering surplus of audacity and a deficit of actual strategy. When pressed on their "exclusive" edge, the response was a vague gesture toward TikTok—a tactic as ubiquitous as it is uninspired.

Professional Misconduct
Beyond the operational failures—the constant chasing to get the listing live, the missed deadlines, and the blatant lies about evening uploads—the personal conduct of the staff was abhorrent. To be met with xenophobic assumptions about my cultural background and racial slurs within my own home is beyond acceptable,  its actually criminal.

The Verdict
Currans attempts to frame basic accountability as "abuse" to deflect from their own failings. They offer nothing that isn't done better, faster, and with more integrity by literally any other agent. They don't do rocket science; they barely manage the basics.
I am relieved to be severed from this agreement. My new agent has achieved in 48 hours what Currans couldn't navigate in weeks.

A fabulous trip, but a very disappointing hire experience.
This was our first time hiring a motorhome, and although we ended up having a fabulous holiday, unfortunately the experience with the company itself left a lot to be desired.

When we arrived to pick up the motorhome there was no one around, and we waited around 15 minutes before a man appeared. He said he was the owner. Partway through the handover he had to leave to collect his son from school, and said he would continue the handover when he returned, which meant everything felt rushed and incomplete. We also noticed quite a lot of damage to the vehicle, despite being told it had “only been out a few times.” There was damage to the table base, to the lid of the hob and the base boards were all scuffed and scraped.

While loading our things, I picked up what I thought was a cleaning rag from inside the bedside wardrobe, but it turned out to be dirty knickers left behind from a previous hire. I was genuinely sickened. The man did apologise and blamed a new cleaner, but that really isn’t an excuse — a basic clean should be guaranteed. I gave him the underwear wrapped in the stained sheet that was on the bed....we had taken our own bedding and I really didn't want to touch theirs.

Once we set off, we did enjoy ourselves. We loved having a bacon butty in the car park at Gretna Green and stopping in the middle of the hills for a cup of tea and a biscuit. However, the tyre pressure alarms went off as soon as we left the yard, and the onboard system kept giving conflicting messages about the water and waste tanks — one minute full, the next empty.

Returning the motorhome was just as chaotic. Again, no one was at the yard. After about 10 minutes the cleaner arrived, but she had no idea how to take delivery of the vehicle. She phoned one of the owners, who told her just to take the keys and they’d check it later. I asked for the phone and spoke to the other owner, this time a lady, and mentioned the dirty knickers, and she again blamed a “new cleaner.” I also mentioned that a driver had stopped us to say the brake lights weren’t working — something we were never told.

We then waited 19 days for our deposit to be returned, only receiving it after chasing twice. For a small business, customer service should be a priority, but sadly it felt severely lacking throughout. I don’t want to hear excuses about new cleaners — train your staff properly from the start and the blame game is just an excuse for arrogance.

We absolutely would hire a motorhome again because we loved the experience itself… but definitely not from this company.

"4 Years of Hell, & ongoing". How long does it take to fit a kitchen properly? - still waiting.
I paid Wickes in 2021 for them to fit my kitchen & utility room, & I'm still waiting for it to be finished, by a 3rd Wickes approved installer.
On 30th September 2024 the 1st installation was eventually (after 2 year & 6 months) ripped out & refitted again for a second time by Wickes installers. Endorsed by the Ombudsman due to how badly it had been fitted 1st time round in March 2022 in only 9 days. It had to be completely re plastered, re tiled & re fitted with new cupboards, & the previous appliances fitted back. This time it was fitted over 3 weeks to give a week for the plaster to dry (instead of less than 24 hours as previous, before fitting wooden cupboards).
Now Wickes has had 2 attempts to install my kitchen & utility room, I feel so very very let down. -The floor and wall tiling has not been done to trading standards (again), disappointed that my utility room sink has not been fitted back in the same place as previous, electric socket not fitted back properly, wall and floor cupboards carcasses & surrounds not level & gaps along inside edge & areas not sealed down properly, skirting board cut into with radiator pipes not secure to wall properly, door frame ripped off before plastering & re fitted back cracked, cheap thin plastic main water supply pipework (installed instead of the original copper) with stop tap too small, plus more issues.
We paid over 20 thousand for this, & it is still not right. It's gone 4 years now from 1st bodge installation, & 1 year 6 months from 2nd bodge installation, overall I've sent Wickes hundreds of emails, plus hundreds of photos & videos from compaints about 1st installation &  complaints about 2nd installation, & have always felt fobbed off when eventually they email back. - Still waiting to know what they intend to do to sort out all the issues from this 2nd installation.
Wickes say they struggled for months to locate another installer saying- 'unfortunately this is proving more difficult than usual as there is a shortage of installers in the area & they are having to look further afield '. However they did find 1 that they have used before, that doesn't live far away at all. They sent around a 3rd installer 4 months ago for site visit to see what needs doing, who seems very nice and keen to do a good job, who could have done it by now - March 2026. But Wickes were not happy him saying our kitchen & utility room needs a full re fit. So Wickes told the installer he had to come back again.- And he did last month, to do a list of materials needed for what Wickes is prepared to do.
Wickes has still not shared with us a list of work that They propose to do, & when, (despite my repeat emails to them). So we Still Have No Date as to when or what year our kitchen & utility room will be finished.
This kitchen installation (my husband & I picked in 2021) was meant to have made me happy, after undergoing many years of cancer treatment. But It's been immensely stressful for over 4 years so far. The excessively long waiting times to receive emails back, & huge delays (of years) Wickes are deliberately taking to try not to resolve issues is disgusting.
My advice to others is, (although the staff seem nice in the shop,) avoid this company for kitchen installations, as the service is not fit for purpose. And Customer Relations is just there to fob the customer off until they give up.

It is with a profound sense of civic alarm and professional distaste that I record my impressions of a recent encounter with a representative of your firm, a technician named "Danny Birkett." While one expects a specialist in vermin disposal to maintain a focus on the mechanical and biological realities of the task, I was instead subjected to a verbal odyssey of the most jarring and prejudiced nature.
Upon my inquiry regarding the ethical and procedural nuances of his work, Mr. Birkett did not offer a technical explanation. Instead, he utilized the opportunity to launch into a protracted and vitriolic monologue concerning the most vulnerable echelons of our society. He spoke with a disturbing lack of empathy about those battling addiction, individuals navigating the complexities of the care system, and those who have endured profound struggle in their personal lives. It was an unprovoked display of hostility toward his fellow man, delivered with the weary condescension of one who believes their own narrow perspective to be an objective truth.
One expects a certain baseline of professional distance and human decency in a service encounter, yet Danny Birkett’s conduct suggests a profound ontological mismatch with any role requiring public interaction. His interpersonal frequency is tuned exclusively to a channel of judgment and derision. To hear a professional representative speak so disparagingly of those facing systemic and personal hardship was nothing short of a masterclass in modern callousness.
Furthermore, having navigated the interpersonal wreckage of other local service providers, I was at least relieved to find that no one named "Jackie" was involved in this particular debacle. It is a small, hollow mercy to know that "PTSD" from her specific brand of passive aggression was not a factor here, though Mr. Birkett’s own verbal vitriol was a more than capable substitute.
In conclusion, I must express my sincere hope that Mr. Birkett’s tenure with your organization is swiftly and decisively terminated, much like the very vermin he is tasked to dispose of. Such a corrosive temperament has no place in a professional setting. I shall look forward to the day I encounter him in a more suitable environment, perhaps at the local "Sainsbury’s," where he might find honest labor stocking shelves, a vocation that mercifully requires no intellectual engagement with the public and offers no platform for his particular brand of social malice. Until that time, I shall be seeking my pest control solutions elsewhere.

⭐ 1 Star – Avoid at all costs

Our problems with Livingway at Edward House started almost immediately after moving in, and the experience only got worse over time.

The heating/AC unit was faulty from the beginning, constantly cutting off. We contacted Livingway for months and were repeatedly told the job had been “put out,” but nothing was ever actually done. By the time summer came, the flat became unbearable — temperatures inside went over 35°C. I even called the emergency line, only to be told it “wasn’t an emergency” and to call back another day. The issue wasn’t resolved until January 2026, nearly a full year after we moved in.

Things escalated further when I came home from a 12-hour shift to find a leak in the flat. When the emergency team attended, they showed me that there had been no hose connected to the back of the unit, meaning it had likely been leaking for months.This could have caused damp and mould in both the living room and bedroom.

When maintenance came out, they initially denied the mould, then simply painted over it with mould paint. As shown in the photos, the mould was still clearly visible. To make matters worse, paint was left all over the carpet inside our flat and even on the carpet outside in the communal area, showing a complete lack of care and professionalism. I took it upon myself to clean this up before we got charged for this during the move out based on other reviews.

The condition of the building itself was also unacceptable — the bin area was absolutely disgusting, constantly overflowing and clearly not maintained properly.

There was also misleading information in the adverts. The listing on Rightmove stated that WiFi was included, which is completely untrue. Even after we gave notice, they have continued advertising the property with WiFi included, despite this not being the case.

We also experienced issues with the rent system being changed, which led to confusion and a backlog of rent through no fault of our own. This added unnecessary stress on top of an already poor experience.

Communication was extremely poor. I specifically asked Livingway to contact my partner during the day, as I work in healthcare and cannot take calls while caring for seriously ill patients. Despite this, they repeatedly called me anyway. Even after explaining my situation, the calls continued.

Other issues included:
•Washing machine breaking and flooding the living room doorway, ruining our towels
•Living room window that wouldn’t lock (reported at 6-month inspection and still not fixed by move-out)
•Wardrobe broken within the first week and left unrepaired for months
•No blinds in any room for almost 3 weeks after we moved in
•Bathroom sink wouldn’t drain without you lifting it

Overall, this has been a stressful and exhausting experience. Basic maintenance, safety issues, and tenant concerns were consistently ignored or poorly handled. I would not recommend renting with Livingway based on our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Integritas. From the Latin word meaning honesty, strong moral principles, and ethical uprightness. I want you to sit with that for a moment while I tell you that I purchased an off-plan property from these people, Sovereign Point, and have spent the last year or two receiving updates that somehow manage to say nothing, promise everything, and deliver less than either.

The updates come in three flavours: vague, vaguer, and "we'll have more news soon." Deadlines have passed without acknowledgment, confident timelines have quietly evaporated, and "soon" has been used so many times it has lost all meaning as a word. I have had to chase countlessly for information that should have been sent proactively, and what I get back when I do could generously be described as creative writing.

Integritas. Someone in that office opened a Latin dictionary, found the most aspirational word they could, and thought: yes, that's us. Remarkable.

The property itself may well be lovely when it eventually exists. But if you're considering buying off-plan from a company whose name literally means integrity, and whose team treats that as more of a loose suggestion than a value, be sure to factor in some patience and a good lawyer.

Costly, Stressful, and Far Less Protection Than Expected.

My experience with Gazeal has been disappointing and ultimately very costly, both financially and emotionally.

The property transaction became heavily delayed, with the seller pushing completion back by around 3 months despite initially appearing willing to exchange much sooner. It could be the estate agent holding off the information, but in any case, in reality, delays of that length create serious complications for buyers - including mortgage offers nearing expiry, additional costs, and ongoing uncertainty across the chain.

What I found most frustrating was that when the seller withdrew from the agreement just 1 day after the reservation contract period ended, this was still ultimately not considered to be 'bad faith' under the process. After going through a lengthy and stressful dispute process, the appeal was unsuccessful, and to make matters worse, I was also ordered to pay additional hearing costs.

Another major concern is the fee structure itself. The buyer pays the reservation fee upfront, whereas the seller only pays their portion if the transaction successfully completes. From my perspective, this creates very little financial risk or commitment for the seller compared to the buyer.

It also became apparent that the agreement is focused primarily around exchange deadlines and appears largely irrelevant to the realities of completion. In practice, a buyer can still face lengthy completion delays, mortgage expiry risks, additional legal and financial costs, and major uncertainty, while remaining with limited practical protection under the agreement.

From my perspective, the level of protection and reassurance promoted by the reservation agreement did not reflect the practical reality when a dispute arises.

My advice to anyone considering this type of agreement:

* Fully understand what protections actually exist in practice. Read the contract thoroughly.
* Carefully consider the risks around delays and mortgage expiry.
* Be aware that proving 'bad faith' appears to be an extremely high threshold.
* Understand that pursuing a dispute can result in additional costs even if you genuinely believe you were treated unfairly.
* Carefully review how the fee structure and contractual timelines actually operate before committing.

While others may have had a different experience, mine was lengthy, stressful, expensive, and ultimately left me feeling far less protected than expected.
